diagnosed_skill_and_repair.overall_diagnosis: The task failures are all attributable to gaps in the D3 visualization skill around building verifier/automation-proof interactive SVGs. Specifically: (1) SVG <text> labels layered over circles intercepted pointer events so Playwright could not click bubbles; (2) the force layout appeared to not spread nodes (bounding boxes showed near-zero x/y spread), implying simulation ticks and position updates were not being applied in a measurable way to rendered geometry at verification time; (3) tooltip show/hide and positioning were unreliable, likely due to event wiring on the wrong layer and brittle coordinate usage. The skill should more explicitly prescribe patterns for layered interactivity, deterministic force-simulation settling, and robust tooltip wiring compatible with Playwright-style tests.

skills.heading: D3.js Visualization Skill
skills.diagnosis: Current guidance is too general for interactive, test-verified SVG bubble/force charts. It does not strongly emphasize that overlay labels/annotations can block pointer events, causing automated clicks to fail. It also under-specifies how to make force simulations deterministic and verifiable via DOM geometry (transforms/cx/cy) at the time tests run, leading to collapsed or unchanged positions even if a simulation exists. Tooltip guidance is not robust enough for grouped nodes and automation (hover targets, visibility toggles, coordinate choice, avoiding CSS that hides/blocks the tooltip).
skills.repair_instruction: Revise/extend the skill with a dedicated section focused on "Automation-proof interactivity & verifiability" that includes: (1) Layering/pointer-events rules: require `pointer-events: none` on non-interactive overlay text/labels; recommend structuring marks as `g.node > circle + text` and attaching click/hover handlers to the circle or the parent `g.node` (not the label), ensuring the intended hit-target is unobstructed. (2) Deterministic force-simulation recipe: set explicit SVG width/height attributes; initialize node positions (optionally seeded near cluster centers); run a fixed number of `simulation.tick()` steps (or run until alpha threshold) after nodes exist; on each tick update rendered positions via `attr('transform', 'translate(x,y)')` on the same element Playwright measures (or update `cx/cy` directly); only then `stop()`; add a quick validation checklist to ensure x/y spread is non-zero and not all nodes share the same transform/cx/cy. (3) Tooltip robustness: standardize on `event.pageX/pageY` (or `clientX/clientY` + scroll) for positioning; ensure show/hide is implemented via explicit CSS classes/opacity and the tooltip has appropriate z-index and `pointer-events: none`; wire `mouseenter/mousemove/mouseleave` (or pointer equivalents) on the interactive node container and ensure filtering logic (e.g., excluding certain categories) doesn’t inadvertently disable all tooltips. (4) Provide a short Playwright-oriented checklist: clickable bubbles (no occlusion), stable selectors/classes/data-* attributes, tooltip appears on hover, selection state reflected via classes/attributes.
